cse404-java/u1.round2:
DEF | 1 | Object-Oriented Programming is a methodology or paradigm to design a program using classes and objects.
MECH | 1 | Programs are organized into objects combining data and code that communicate with each other through message passing.
SPEC | 1 | The book lists seven basic concepts: Object, Class, Data abstraction, Data encapsulation, Inheritance, Polymorphism, and Dynamic binding.
STEP | 1 | Conceptualize BankAccount as an object combining state like balance and behavior like deposit and withdrawal operations.
THIN | 1 | no
DEF | 2 | History of Java describes the creation and evolution of the language initiated by James Gosling and the Green Team at Sun Microsystems in 1991.
MECH | 2 | Java source code is compiled into platform-independent bytecode that is dynamically verified and executed by the Java Virtual Machine.
SPEC | 2 | Java was initially named Oak before being renamed Java in 1995 when incorporated by Netscape.
STEP | 2 | Note that the BankAccount class source file compiles into bytecode executable across different operating system JVMs.
THIN | 2 | no
DEF | 3 | Data types represent the different values to be stored in a variable.
MECH | 3 | Primitive data types directly store raw values in memory, whereas non-primitive data types store references to objects.
SPEC | 3 | Java defines eight primitive data types: boolean (1 bit), byte (1 byte), char (2 bytes), short (2 bytes), int (4 bytes), long (8 bytes), float (4 bytes), and double (8 bytes).
STEP | 3 | Choose double for the balance field and int for the account ID field of BankAccount.
THIN | 3 | no
DEF | 4 | A variable is a name of a memory location used to hold data of a declared type during program execution.
MECH | 4 | Declaring a variable allocates memory according to its type, assigning default zero or false values to primitives and null to reference objects.
SPEC | 4 | Java classifies variables into three types: local variable, instance variable, and static variable.
STEP | 4 | Declare instance variables balance and accountNumber alongside a static variable accountCount inside BankAccount.
THIN | 4 | no
DEF | 5 | A constant is a variable whose value cannot be changed after declaration during program execution.
MECH | 5 | Java uses the final keyword to lock variable assignment, causing any attempt to reassign the value to generate a compile-time error.
SPEC | 5 | The syntax form within a class is modifier static final dataType variableName = value.
STEP | 5 | Declare a private static final constant MINIMUM_BALANCE in BankAccount to enforce an unalterable minimum balance floor.
THIN | 5 | no
DEF | 6 | Comments are statements that are not executed by the compiler and interpreter, written to provide information or explanations to human readers.
MECH | 6 | The compiler ignores single-line and multi-line comments, while the javadoc tool extracts documentation comments to generate HTML API documentation.
SPEC | 6 | Java provides three comment types: Single Line Comment (//), Multi Line Comment (/* */), and Documentation Comment (/** */).
STEP | 6 | Add documentation comments above the BankAccount class definition and its constructors to document their functionality.
THIN | 6 | no
DEF | 7 | Operators are special symbols used in expressions to perform operations on operands.
MECH | 7 | Binary operators compute values from operands, and compound assignment operators evaluate expressions before storing results directly back into the variable.
SPEC | 7 | Shorthand assignment operators include +=, -=, *=, /=, and %=.
STEP | 7 | Apply the += shorthand operator inside a deposit method to add incoming funds directly to the balance field.
THIN | 7 | no
DEF | 8 | Type conversion and casting convert a value from one compatible or incompatible data type to another.
MECH | 8 | Widening conversion automatically promotes smaller compatible types to larger destination types, whereas narrowing requires explicit casting syntax for incompatible or larger-to-smaller assignments.
SPEC | 8 | The automatic widening hierarchy is byte -> short -> int -> long -> float -> double.
STEP | 8 | Explicitly cast a floating-point interest calculation to double when adding earned interest to the account balance.
THIN | 8 | no
DEF | 9 | Control structures direct the execution flow of a program through selection decisions and iterative loops.
MECH | 9 | Conditional statements evaluate boolean expressions to branch execution, while loop statements repeat execution until a controlling condition becomes false.
SPEC | 9 | The jump statements break and continue exit a loop entirely or skip immediately to its next iteration.
STEP | 9 | Implement an if conditional statement in a withdraw method to confirm the balance exceeds the requested withdrawal amount.
THIN | 9 | no
DEF | 10 | A class is a logical template or blueprint from which object instances sharing common properties and behaviors are created.
MECH | 10 | Memory for a class instance is dynamically allocated using the new operator, and instance members are accessed using the dot operator on object references.
SPEC | 10 | General class declaration syntax uses the class keyword followed by the class name and a curly-brace delimited class body containing variable and method declarations.
STEP | 10 | Define the BankAccount class block, instantiate an object using new BankAccount(), and access its members via the dot operator.
THIN | 10 | no
DEF | 11 | Method overloading is the capability of defining multiple methods within the same class that share the same name but different parameter lists.
MECH | 11 | The Java compiler resolves overloaded method calls by matching the number, types, and sequence of argument values provided in the call.
SPEC | 11 | Overloaded methods must differ in their parameter signatures; differing solely by return type is invalid.
STEP | 11 | Overload the deposit method to accept either a single double amount or both a double amount and a String description parameter.
THIN | 11 | no
DEF | 12 | A constructor is a special member method used to initialize newly created objects of a class upon instantiation.
MECH | 12 | A constructor shares the exact class name, has no return type, and executes automatically when an object is instantiated via the new operator.
SPEC | 12 | Java supports default constructors with no arguments, parameterized constructors, and constructor overloading.
STEP | 12 | Provide a default constructor initializing balance to zero and an overloaded parameterized constructor accepting an initial deposit, using this to disambiguate parameters from instance variables.
THIN | 12 | no
DEF | 13 | String handling encompasses creating and manipulating character sequences using String, StringBuffer, and StringBuilder classes.
MECH | 13 | String instances store immutable character sequences in memory, whereas StringBuffer and StringBuilder objects provide mutable sequences that can be modified dynamically.
SPEC | 13 | The String class provides methods like charAt(), concat(), equals(), length(), and substring().
STEP | 13 | Use StringBuilder within an account summary method to build and return a formatted String representation of the BankAccount state.
THIN | 13 | no
